content.label: Examiner note - acids and bases trade protons
content.body: The theory of record: an acid is a proton donor, a base a proton acceptor. In HCl + NH3 -> NH4+ + Cl-, the chloride ion is what is left when the acid has donated its proton, and the base NH3 becomes NH4+ - so ammonia is a base even though it carries no OH- at all. Metal oxides and hydroxides accept protons too; alkalis are simply the bases that dissolve in water.
